title: NASA announces Artemis III crew for next phase of moon program
facts: NASA officially announced the four astronauts assigned to the upcoming Artemis III moon mission.
The Artemis III crew is expected to launch into Earth orbit next year to test rendezvous and docking procedures with moon landers.
SpaceX and Blue Origin are currently building the moon landers designated for the Artemis lunar program.
NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman introduced the Artemis III crew members at the Johnson Space Center in Houston.
Bob Hines was officially named as the backup crew member for the Artemis III mission.
Astronaut Bresnik logged 149 days in space during a space shuttle flight in 2009 and a long-duration stay on the International Space Station in 2017.
Astronaut Parmitano previously served as the first Italian commander of the International Space Station.
Astronaut Douglas will be making his first career space flight on the Artemis III mission.
Astronaut Douglas previously served as a backup crew member for the Artemis II around-the-moon mission.
Astronaut Rubio spent a U.S. record 371 days in space aboard the International Space Station in 2022-2023.
The Artemis III crew will launch atop a Space Launch System rocket inside an Orion capsule.
The Artemis III mission is currently the only test flight NASA is planning before a moon landing attempt scheduled for 2028.
Blue Origin suffered a catastrophic launch pad explosion on May 28 that destroyed a New Glenn rocket.
NASA aims to begin construction of a moon base near the lunar south pole in the 2029-2030 timeframe.
The Artemis II crew successfully completed a flight around the moon in April of 2026.
